result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that the studio is underpriced and give a specific new price with a stepwise test. A covers more of the rubric: it tracks both close rate and waitlist length, handles existing quotes and repeat or referral clients, and gives correct break-even arithmetic. B offers more ways to charge more (tiers, rush fees, paid revisions), but it says nothing about repeat clients and relies on unsupported market benchmarks such as a 40-60% close rate and buyers paying 'several times $1,800'. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that the waitlist and close rate mean the price is too low, and both name a specific new price. B is better on stepwise testing: it explicitly tracks both close rate and waitlist length. It also covers repeat and referral clients, and its break-even table shows why the risk is small. A offers more ways to charge more (tiers, rush fees, paid revisions), but it skips repeat clients, and its market claims about competitor prices and normal close rates are unsupported.
